newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks rally on Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks rally on Greenspan testimony.

text.p: Stock prices extended their drive into record ground Tuesday as investors put a positive spin on comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 41.95 points at 6,885.82, building on Monday's record finish of 6,843.87. The New York Stock Exchange's curbs on programme trading were activated when the index gained 50 points in early afternoon.
In the broader market, advances and declines were about even on moderate volume of 338 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 11.99 points at 1,376.27, which also beat Monday's record of 1,364.28. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.20 at 590.14.

Prior to the start of Greenspan's testimony on the economy at a Senate budget committee hearing, the Dow index had been down more than 40 points as Wall Street turned cautious, recalling the Fed chief's comments in December about the "irrational exuberance" of financial markets that sent stock prices reeling.
"It seems that markets discounted the absolutely worst from Greenspan, but his testimony was rather benign," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal & Co.

"Investors were afraid of a repeat of his 'irrational exuberance' comment," he said. "Instead, they got a positive comment on restrained consumer spending and the increased amounts of money in savings and investments."
LaTronica said, "The testimony was much more positive than had been anticipated and that is why we had our reversal today in the Dow industrials."
Greenspan delivered an upbeat assesment of the economy but he also warned of the risks of wage-driven inflation in the future.
He also observed, "The stock market continues to climb at a breathtaking rate."
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said Greenspan indicated the Fed was only doing its job and remaining vigilant for inflation.

"He did not say anything new. He said that Fed remains vigilant and that we might be coming to the end of the period of low wages," Cardillo said. "These aren't new words. The Fed's job is to reassure people it is alert and that if anything changes in the economy it would take action."
Cardillo said now that the testimony was out of the way, the market was resuming its focus on earnings and special situations.

Among the winners, Boeing was up 5 at 111-1/2 after the aircraft maker announced late Monday that market conditions do not support ongoing development of larger version of Boeing's 747 Jumbo Jet. Boeing instead plans to focus attention on developing new versions of its 767 and 777 twin-engine jets.
International Business Machines jumped 2-1/8 to 168-1/8 on speculation that it would release strong fourth quarter earnings, when it reports its results after the close of trading.
Among special situations, Target Therapeutics Inc. rallied 10-3/8 to 69-3/8 on news that the company will be acquired by Boston Scientific Corp. for about $70 per share in Boston Scientific stock.
